message.reasoning_content:
The user wants a translation of C# code to Kotlin.
The C# code reads two integers n and k, then a string s.
It checks if any character in s appears more than k times.
If so, prints "NO" and exits.
Otherwise, prints "YES".

Constraints:
- No extra description or tokens.
- Only the translated code.

Kotlin implementation details:
- Use `readLine()` for input.
- Split and parse integers.
- Iterate string.
- Count occurrences. Can use `count { it == s[i] }` or a frequency map for efficiency, but the original is O(n^2), so a direct translation is fine, though idiomatic Kotlin would use a map. I'll stick to the logic but write it idiomatically enough.
- `return` in main exits the program.

Structure:
```kotlin
fun main() {
    val (n, k) = readLine()!!.split(' ').map { it.toInt() }
    val s = readLine()!!
    for (i in s.indices) {
        var c = 0
        for (j in s.indices) {
            if (s[i] == s[j]) c++
        }
        if (c > k) {
            print("NO")
            return
        }
    }
    println("YES")
}
```
Note: The variable `n` is read but not used in the logic, just like the C# code. I'll keep it to match the input parsing.

source_data.prob_desc_description: One day Kefa found n baloons. For convenience, we denote color of i-th baloon as si — lowercase letter of the Latin alphabet. Also Kefa has k friends. Friend will be upset, If he get two baloons of the same color. Kefa want to give out all baloons to his friends. Help Kefa to find out, can he give out all his baloons, such that no one of his friens will be upset — print «YES», if he can, and «NO», otherwise. Note, that Kefa's friend will not upset, if he doesn't get baloons at all.
source_data.prob_desc_output_spec: Answer to the task — «YES» or «NO» in a single line. You can choose the case (lower or upper) for each letter arbitrary.
source_data.prob_desc_input_spec: The first line contains two integers n and k (1 ≤ n, k ≤ 100) — the number of baloons and friends. Next line contains string s — colors of baloons.
source_data.prob_desc_notes: NoteIn the first sample Kefa can give 1-st and 3-rd baloon to the first friend, and 2-nd and 4-th to the second.In the second sample Kefa needs to give to all his friends baloons of color a, but one baloon will stay, thats why answer is «NO».
